change_summary: Added an audit-only script that reruns the current accepted stack on the three fixed OHLCV snapshots and measures 5/10/20 trading-day returns after every `exit_reason == target`, grouped by strategy, sector, and 20-day relative strength versus SPY/QQQ. No production strategy code was changed.

delta_metrics.decision_basis: The audit found pockets of continuation, but all-target continuation was not stable across windows. This creates a follow-up screen for breakout Energy/Commodities target width but does not justify a production rule by itself.

hypothesis: After accepted Technology/Commodity trend target-width repairs and the 25% single-position cap, target winners may still contain continuation alpha after exit. If target exits keep rising across fixed windows, a future re-entry or hold-extension rule may be worth testing.

llm_metrics.blocker_relation: LLM soft-ranking remains blocked by candidate-level replay coverage; this deterministic audit does not change LLM responsibilities.

market_regime_summary.late_strong: slow-melt bull where target exits continued on average
market_regime_summary.mid_weak: rotation-heavy bull where target exits did not continue on average
market_regime_summary.old_thin: mixed-to-weak tape where target exits were nearly flat after exit

next_retry_requires: Do not promote generic post-target re-entry or hold-extension from this audit
If continuation is revisited, require a sleeve-specific rule with multi-window exposure and EV validation
Use breakout Energy/Commodities target-width only as a narrow follow-up screen, not as a generic continuation doctrine
notes: This was alpha_search through mechanism audit, not bug repair. It changed no production logic.
rejection_reason: Audit-only result; no production rule was tested or promoted. Broad post-target continuation is explicitly not supported because mid_weak post-target average return was negative.
